bull.b: The AP3 platform gives Acrivon a differentiated research approach centered on matching treatments to patient response signatures. If validated clinically, this precision-oncology capability could improve development decisions, support targeted therapies, and create a durable basis for advancing multiple programs.

Very low leverage and positive stockholders’ equity provide greater financial flexibility than a highly debt-funded biotechnology model. This reduces fixed financing pressure and leaves the company better positioned to direct available resources toward clinical development and platform advancement.

A pipeline of investigational oncology medicines gives Acrivon multiple potential routes to generate future clinical value rather than relying on a single disclosed candidate. Continued trial progress could expand the platform’s commercial opportunity if candidates demonstrate meaningful patient benefit.

bear.b: Acrivon has no marketed-product revenue, so its operations remain dependent on advancing unapproved candidates toward regulatory and commercial milestones. Until that transition occurs, the business lacks operating revenue to offset research costs or demonstrate established commercial demand.

Sustained negative operating and free cash flow means the company consumes capital while funding its clinical programs. This ongoing burn can reduce financial flexibility over time and increases the importance of securing additional resources to maintain development activities.

Large recurring net losses show that Acrivon currently has no earnings base supporting its operations and remains far from profitability. The persistence of these losses can accelerate equity and asset erosion, limiting the company’s ability to fund growth internally.
